transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... well, I've just been having some trouble at work lately. I keep making... I don't know, dumb mistakes on the sales reports. Like, copying the wrong numbers down from the team dashboard. Or I'll miss a line in a procedure I was supposed to check... even when I thought I already went over it. So, yeah. That's why I'm here.
How long have you been experiencing these mistakes at work? Did this start suddenly, or has it been gradually getting worse over time?
Um... I guess it's been a while. But it really became a problem when I moved into the supervisor role. That was about... a year and two months ago.
Besides these mistakes at work, how has your mood been over this past year or so? Have you been feeling sad, anxious, or down?
No, not really. I mean, I get frustrated sometimes about the mistakes, but... I wouldn't say I'm sad or anything. Just normal, I guess.
When you're making these mistakes at work, do you find it hard to focus or concentrate on the task, or is it more that you forget things you've already learned or checked?

Um... I guess it's more the focus. Like, when I'm trying to review call notes or the numbers... if there's a conversation across the room, or I just have a random thought about something at home... I just get pulled off track. I don't really even notice it happening right away. So... yeah, it's that.
Do you find yourself feeling restless or fidgety during the day, or do you have trouble sitting still for extended periods?

Yeah, I guess. I mean... sitting through long meetings is tough. It kind of feels like... I don't know, like my body is just buzzing inside. I end up shifting around a lot, or... tapping my foot. Sometimes I just make up an excuse to get up for a minute.

Looking back to when you were a child or teenager in school, did you ever have similar problems with focus or concentration, or did teachers ever mention that you had trouble paying attention in class?

Yeah, I guess so. I mean... my mom still brings it up sometimes. She kept these old notes from my elementary school teachers. They always said I was rushing through my work, or... losing my homework. Stuff like that. And I guess I talked out of turn a lot, or couldn't stay in my seat unless they told me to. So... yeah, it's been a thing for a while, I suppose.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with lifelong history of inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity dating back to elementary school (teacher reports of rushing through work, losing homework, talking out of turn, difficulty staying seated). Current symptoms include difficulty sustaining attention during work tasks (easily distracted by conversations or random thoughts), restlessness with internal buzzing sensation, fidgeting, and foot-tapping. Functional impairment is evident in supervisor role with repeated work mistakes. Symptoms are not attributable to mood disorder (denies sadness/anxiety) or recent stressor (symptoms predate supervisor role by years). Clinical presentation is consistent with Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder, Combined Type.
